https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/pu.label: QuantLib
https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/pu.body: the C++ quantitative finance library had a `NaN` in its Gauss-Laguerre quadrature. Past order ~200, one of the weights underflows to exactly `0.0`, and `inf × 0` is `NaN` in IEEE 754. The fix re-derives the weight in log-space so the underflow no longer occurs. It is tested against the real consumer (`AnalyticHestonEngine`) and was independently re-derived in NumPy as a check.

https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools/p.label: edgartools
https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools/p.body: a much smaller fix. The quickstart stated Python 3.8 while `pyproject.toml` required 3.10, and the docs recommended a `cash_flow_statement()` alias that is deprecated for removal in v6.0. No math, only documentation that gave new users incorrect information. Merged.

https://github.com/ever-co/ever-gauzy/pu.label: ever-gauzy
https://github.com/ever-co/ever-gauzy/pu.body: a null-prototype object, a pattern used to avoid prototype-pollution bugs, crashed the utility function written to guard against prototype pollution. `Object.create(null)` has no `.constructor` to read `.name` from. The fix is one `getPrototypeOf` check. Merged.

https://github.com/ever-co/ever-gauzy/pu.label: ever-gauzy
https://github.com/ever-co/ever-gauzy/pu.body: the project's security-disclosure badge pointed at a domain that no longer resolves (DNS `SERVFAIL`, not a 404, which most link-checkers miss). The broken link was on the line explaining how to report a security issue, so it seemed worth fixing quickly. Merged.

https://github.com/dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib.label: Riskfolio-Lib
https://github.com/dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib.body: the constructor defined its own `returns` setter, including a type check, then bypassed it with `self._returns = returns`, so no validation ran. A single `NaN` in the input data does not fail at construction. It fails four stack frames deep inside `scipy.linalg.eigh`, with a message that has nothing to do with the actual data.

https://github.com/dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib.label: Riskfolio-Lib
https://github.com/dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib.body: `Axes.plot_date` and `matplotlib.cm.get_cmap` were both removed in Matplotlib 3.11, but `requirements.txt` still says `>=3.9.2`. Anyone on a current install hits an `AttributeError` when plotting a portfolio.

https://github.com/rburkholder/trade-fra.label: trade-frame
https://github.com/rburkholder/trade-fra.body: 37 images in the README that were never images: `![text](path)` pointing at `.h` files and directories, which render as broken icons. Two of the targets had also been renamed `.h` → `.hpp` years earlier and the doc was never updated.

https://github.com/rburkholder/trade-fra.label: trade-frame
https://github.com/rburkholder/trade-fra.body: asked where the meaning of an IQFeed trade-condition code comes from. Answer: nowhere in the repo, on purpose. IQFeed publishes the code table live over the same socket connection, so a hardcoded copy would go stale. Documented that mechanism instead of adding a table.

https://github.com/AsthaMishra/matching-.label: matching-engine
https://github.com/AsthaMishra/matching-.body: an out-of-range price and a malformed one were rejected with the identical error reason, so when debugging real order flow the log gave no way to tell which one had happened.

https://github.com/vollib/py_lets_be_rat.label: py_lets_be_rational
https://github.com/vollib/py_lets_be_rat.body: no `LICENSE` file, which blocks `conda-forge` packaging for everyone downstream.

https://github.com/vollib/cody-special/p.label: cody-special
https://github.com/vollib/cody-special/p.body: `erf_cody` and `normaldistribution` were split into their own files, and the `@numba.njit` decoration that made them fast was not carried over.

https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultra.label: jev-ultrafast
https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultra.body: the agent's browser target opens on `about:blank`, which is already `readyState == 'complete'` before the real navigation starts. The first poll after `Page.navigate` could read that stale state and give the policy a page that never loaded. The run then terminates as `BLOCKED` in under a second, which looks like the agent failing when the harness never observed anything real.

https://github.com/wangzhe3224/awesome-s.label: awesome-systematic-trading
https://github.com/wangzhe3224/awesome-s.body: checked all ~650 links in the list against the GitHub API and actual DNS resolution, not just an HTTP status code (which often gives false positives when sites block bots). Six repos were genuinely gone. No replacements were guessed for the ones without a verified successor.

https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/pull/2.label: microsoft/qlib
https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/pull/2.body: Microsoft's quant research platform (48k+ stars) threw a `DeprecationWarning` on `import qlib`, because a module-level constant was built with `pd.Timedelta("1day")` instead of the explicit-unit form. Same value, no warning, one-line fix.

https://github.com/domokane/FinancePy/pu.label: domokane/FinancePy
https://github.com/domokane/FinancePy/pu.body: `np.any(volatility) < 0.0`. `np.any()` on a non-empty array is already a bool before it meets the `< 0.0`, so the negative-volatility guard on FX option greeks could never fire. The sibling `delta()` method got this right (`np.any(v < 0.0)`); this one did not. Found by asking why two methods on the same class disagreed about how to validate the same input.

https://github.com/pst-group/pysystemtra.label: pysystemtrade
https://github.com/pst-group/pysystemtra.body: two collection-breaking bugs unrelated to each other. One: a wildcard import three layers deep replaced `datetime` the class with `datetime` the module, so `datetime.strptime(...)` failed with an error that looks like a typo but is a namespace collision, hard to spot from the file that crashed. Two: an unescaped `\n` inside a docstring was interpreted as a real newline at parse time, which Python 3.12's doctest parser treated as an indentation problem.

https://github.com/ranaroussi/quantstats.label: ranaroussi/quantstats
https://github.com/ranaroussi/quantstats.body: `cagr()` computed `abs(total + 1.0) ** (1/years) - 1`. With `compounded=False`, summed returns can go below −100%, and `abs()` flips negative terminal wealth positive, turning a −240% loss into a reported **+40% CAGR**. Confirmed and fixed directly by the maintainer in v0.0.82: "this release exists because of these reports." (fixed upstream in v0.0.82).
